title: Text editors
subtitle: Vim modes, nano bindings, EDITOR, and visudo

cards.meaning: Set the default editor for tools that open one
cards.notes: Honored by visudo, crontab -e, git commit (and VISUAL). On a server you live in an editor.

cards.meaning: Open file in Vim — starts in Command (Normal) mode
cards.notes: Vim = Vi IMproved. Always expect vi/vim on Unix. Learn with vimtutor.

cards.meaning: Vim’s three modes: keys are commands, text, or Ex commands
cards.notes: Type to change the file only in Insert. Esc always returns to Command.

cards.meaning: Move left / down / up / right (Command mode)
cards.notes: Inverted-T navigation. Also: w/b word, 0/$ line ends, gg/G file start/end.

cards.meaning: Jump to first / last line of the file
cards.notes: Memory hook: gg ground floor, G Ground of the file (the end).

cards.meaning: Delete (cut) line / yank (copy) line / paste after
cards.notes: Double letter = whole line. P pastes before. Also x = delete char, dw = delete word.

cards.meaning: Insert before cursor / append after / new line below / above
cards.notes: All enter Insert from Command. Esc to leave Insert.
?pattern searches backward. N = previous match. Same idea as less.

cards.meaning: Write / quit / save+quit / quit discarding changes
cards.notes: Panic combo: Esc then :wq. :q fails if unsaved. :!command runs a shell command.

cards.meaning: Modeless editor — ordinary keys type text; cheatsheet on screen
cards.notes: ^ = Ctrl, M- = Alt/Cmd. Easier than vim for beginners.

cards.meaning: Save / exit / search / cut line / paste (uncut)
cards.notes: M-6 copies the line without cutting. Kill/uncut = cut/paste.

cards.meaning: Edit /etc/sudoers with a syntax check on save
cards.notes: Never edit sudoers with a normal editor. A typo can lock you out of sudo. Ubuntu often opens nano.
